def move(terrain, start, duration_s, n_runs, seed):
    import numpy as np
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)

    N = 60
    dt = duration_s / (N - 1)
    t_array = np.linspace(0, duration_s, N)
    # Initialize points: shape (n_runs, 60, 3) [lat, lon, t]
    points = np.empty((n_runs, N, 3), dtype=float)
    points[:, :, 2] = t_array  # time is same for all runs

    # Start positions
    lat0 = np.full(n_runs, start[0], dtype=float)
    lon0 = np.full(n_runs, start[1], dtype=float)
    points[:, 0, 0] = lat0
    points[:, 0, 1] = lon0

    # Fixed direction: due south bearing = 180° = pi rad
    bearing = np.pi

    # We want walkers to veer due south, experiment with slope usage:
    # 217% fraction slope >30deg means frequent steep terrain
    # We'll modulate speed by local slope and uphill/downhill

    # Terrain params
    m_lat = terrain.m_lat
    m_lon = terrain.m_lon
    cell_m = terrain.cell_m

    # Set a target average speed ~1.3 m/s typical human walking, slower uphill, faster downhill

    # To approximate published dist stats (median ~2.86 km in duration_s seconds)
    # approximate average speed needed:
    avg_speed_mps = 2860 / duration_s  # ~1.43 m/s for duration_s=2000, e.g.

    # To induce spread, add some per-run speed factor lognormal ~ (mean=1, sd=0.3)
    speed_factors = rng.lognormal(mean=0, sigma=0.25, size=n_runs)
    # Clamp speed factors to [0.7, 1.5]
    speed_factors = np.clip(speed_factors, 0.7, 1.5)

    # Preallocate lat, lon arrays
    lat = np.empty((n_runs, N), dtype=float)
    lon = np.empty((n_runs, N), dtype=float)
    lat[:, 0] = lat0
    lon[:, 0] = lon0

    # For each time step move each walker
    # Compute horizontal step in meters = approx speed * dt
    # But speed depends on slope incline between points (approximate by slope_deg at last position),
    # and characteristic to this hypothesis is steep slopes may attract or challenge - so modulate speed

    # We model:
    # - base speed = avg_speed_mps * speed_factor
    # - modulated by a factor depending on slope_deg: slow where slope<10°, fastest near 35°, slower again near 60+°
    # Fit smooth speed multiplier as a piecewise: peak speed at 30-40 deg slope in [1..3] m/s range, 
    # but capped by Tobler formula (terrain.tobler_speed_ms)

    # Precompute the bearings arrays for offset
    # All moves due south => bearing fixed per all steps.

    # We need elevations to compute d_elev between steps: elevation at start and next pos

    # Start loop over segments (t=0 to t=1,...59)

    # To avoid Python loop over runs, we loop over time steps only (59), vector over runs.

    for i in range(1, N):
        lat_i_1 = lat[:, i-1]
        lon_i_1 = lon[:, i-1]

        slope_deg = terrain.slope_deg(lat_i_1, lon_i_1)

        # Speed multiplier function:
        # Use a Gaussian-like hump centered at 35 degrees slope with width ~15 deg:
        # max multiplier ~1.6, min ~0.5
        slope_center = 35
        slope_width = 15
        slope_factor = 0.5 + 1.1 * np.exp(-0.5 * ((slope_deg - slope_center)/slope_width)**2)
        # Clamp factor to [0.5,1.6]
        slope_factor = np.clip(slope_factor, 0.5, 1.6)

        # Compute elevation differences approximated as slope * cell_m in m vertical,
        # slope_deg = arctan(d_elev/d_horizontal) * 180/pi
        # d_elev = tan(slope_rad) * cell_m
        slope_rad = slope_deg * np.pi / 180
        d_elev = np.tan(slope_rad) * cell_m  # approximate vertical delta going south

        # horizontal step distance ~ speed * dt (meters)
        base_speed = avg_speed_mps * speed_factors * slope_factor

        # Tobler speed correction for local slope:
        # Horizontal step distance per dt guess:
        # Tobler speed = terrain.tobler_speed_ms(d_elev, cell_m) in m/s
        # Use Tobler as multiplicative factor (clip to [0.2,4.0] m/s)
        tobler_speed = terrain.tobler_speed_ms(d_elev, cell_m)
        tobler_speed = np.clip(tobler_speed, 0.2, 4.0)

        # Final speed is mean of base_speed and tobler_speed, to respect terrain physics:
        speed = 0.5 * (base_speed + tobler_speed)
        # Clamp to [0.3, 2.5] for sensible walking speeds
        speed = np.clip(speed, 0.3, 2.5)

        dist_m = speed * dt

        # offset position by dist_m due south (bearing = π)
        lat_new, lon_new = terrain.offset(lat_i_1, lon_i_1, bearing, dist_m)

        # Clamp into terrain box
        lat_new, lon_new = terrain.clamp(lat_new, lon_new)

        # Store new positions
        lat[:, i] = lat_new
        lon[:, i] = lon_new

    # Compose points array lat, lon, time
    points[:, :, 0] = lat
    points[:, :, 1] = lon

    # Check inside terrain box all points per run
    inside_all = terrain.inside(points[:, :, 0], points[:, :, 1])
    ok = np.all(inside_all, axis=1)

    return points, ok
